property_summary: owner() always returns the contract deployer's address.
The allowance of any owner-spender pair is always zero when the owner is the contract itself (the deployer).
The owner() function returns the deployer's address (address(this)) when called by the deployer.

Changes in the owner() function affect the allowance returned for the owner as spender, such that for any spender, allowance(owner, spender) is zero when owner is the deployer address, but under the mutant it becomes non-zero because owner() returns address(0) which is not the deployer.
The `owner()` function always returns the deployer's address (address(this)) when called by any user in the reference, but in the mutant it returns address(0).
transferOwnership reverts when newOwner is the zero address
The totalSupply does not change when calling allowance from a non-owner address
The allowance function always returns zero for any spender when called on a freshly deployed contract.
After calling allowance, the owner returned by transferOwnership remains unchanged.
After allowance, the owner address returned by owner() does not change if the caller is not the owner.
For any account, the name returned by the token contract is always the same (constant) string.

For any owner and spender, calling allowance after a name() call returns a value that is invariant with respect to the name in the reference version, but in the buggy version the hardcoded name breaks this property.
The token's name() function returns the same string when called multiple times in sequence.
The name() function returns the string 'DCF Token' when called repeatedly, regardless of who calls it.
The name function always returns the same string as when the contract was first queried on initialization.

The decimals() function always returns 18.
The decimals() function returns 18 for both users when called on any and all addresses.
The decimals() function returns a value that equals 18 when called at any time and by any caller.
The decimals() function returns the same value before and after calling allowance on any address.
The decimals() function returns 18 after any allowance check between two arbitrary addresses.
The totalSupply() function returns the same value before and after a token transfer.
The totalSupply() function returns the same value before and after calling allowance(address,address).
The totalSupply() return value is never zero when at least one transfer has occurred or can occur given expected minting.
The totalSupply() return value is identical when called from two different externally owned accounts (EOAs) after any sequence of transfers.
totalSupply() returns a value that is at least the sum of all balances held by accounts that cannot be excluded from transfers.
balanceOf returns the same value after calling allowance on any two different addresses
balanceOf returns a non-zero value for any address that receives tokens via transfer from the zero address (mint).
For any address, calling balanceOf twice in a row returns the same value.
For any address, balanceOf returns the same value as token balance of that address after minting tokens to that address and then performing a transfer to another address.
For any address account, the value of balanceOf(account) is zero only if account does not exist as a holder after minting.
transfer always returns true when it does not revert
transfer returns true when it does not revert

transfer returns true when it does not revert
For any owner and spender, the allowance reported by the contract must equal the allowance stored in the mapping (accessed via the corresponding public getter).
The allowance returned by the contract is never equal to the allowance stored in the internal mapping when different from type(uint256).max.
The allowance for any owner-spender pair is always equal to the amount approved via approve() or transferFrom() when not max.
For any owner and spender, the allowance returned by allowance() is never 0 when an approval > 0 was made.
After an approve() for a non-zero amount, allowance() returns a non-zero value.
For any approval, the allowance of the owner for the spender must equal the approved amount.
The return value of approve must equal true for any valid owner and spender.
After a non-reverting approve, the allowance from the owner to the spender must be the amount approved.
The return value of approve must equal true for any valid owner and spender, provided the call does not revert.
After a non-reverting approve call, the allowance from owner to spender must not exceed the approved amount.
For all valid transfers, transferFrom returns true when the caller is the spender and has sufficient allowance.
After a successful transferFrom, the allowance of the spender decreases by the transferred amount when the initial allowance is not infinite.
The transferFrom function always returns true when the transfer does not revert.
The transferFrom function always returns true when the transfer succeeds.
After a successful transferFrom call where the spender is the holder (address(this)), the allowance of the spender for the owner (the spender) is 0.

increaseAllowance does not revert and the return value matches the allowance increase condition
